It was the spring of 1986. President Ronald Reagan had just delivered a
national address
[pleading](https://www.reaganlibrary.gov/archives/speech/address-nation-
situation-nicaragua) with Congress to give $100 million in military aid to the
Contras - a right-wing paramilitary group seeking to overthrow the socialist
Nicaraguan government - whom he once
[called](https://www.reaganlibrary.gov/archives/speech/remarks-annual-dinner-
conservative-political-action-conference) the moral equivalent of America's
founding fathers.

Next, he launched strikes in Libya - causing domestic and international
frustration, as the administration only notified Congress once the planes were
airborne.

Involvement in Libya was an easier pill than Nicaragua for his opponents to
swallow. Reagan attempted to use that reality to rally support for both
efforts.

In remarks at a Heritage Foundation dinner, Reagan
[claimed](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-the-heritage-
foundation-anniversary-dinner) the Nicaraguan Sandinistas were "training,
supporting, and directing, as well as sheltering terrorists; and in this
sense, they're trying to build a Libya on our doorstep." Conversely, he said,
it was "the Contras, the freedom fighters, who are stopping them."

This language did not come out of nowhere. Around that time, Reagan
[read](https://www.jta.org/archive/after-discussing-netanyahu-book-with-
reagan-poindexter-said-he-avoided-mentioning-fund-for-contras) a manual of
sorts: _Terrorism: How the West Can Win_ - a collection edited by Israel's
representative to the United Nations, a young diplomat in his late 30s named
Benjamin Netanyahu.

The book and its contributors focus on Libya as a nexus of terror, and
"communist totalitarianism and Islamic (and Arab) radicalism" as harbors of
terrorism, as they make self-serving distinctions between "freedom fighters"
and "terrorists" - emphasizing the necessity to support the former, often
fiercely against the latter.

Reagan's then-National Security Adviser John Poindexter (who at the time was
orchestrating the covert sale of U.S. weapons to Iran, to illegally divert the
money to fund the Contras in what is known now as the Iran-Contra scandal)
[told](https://archive.org/details/Iran-
ContraHearingsTestimonyTranscripts/1987-irn-0007_Poindexter/page/50/mode/2up)
Congress about the president's interest in the book.

During a 1987 hearing, Poindexter recounted an episode on a flight in May
1986. He claimed that, after he and Reagan talked about Netanyahu's book, the
president asked if there was anything he could do "unilaterally" to back the
Contras, despite an explicit congressional ban on funding the group. Here,
Poindexter testified, is when he considered telling Reagan about the Iran-
Contra scheme, but opted not to, to save him from political embarrassment.

A month after that episode, in June, the International Court of Justice, or
the United Nations' World Court,
[ruled](https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1986/06/28/world-
court-says-us-violates-international-law-by-aiding-
contras/8aedb6b7-4461-4686-b5e5-af9870028751/) that the U.S. had violated
international law by backing the Contras.

The Reagan State Department rejected the ruling and
[said](https://www.nytimes.com/1986/06/28/world/world-court-supports-
nicaragua-after-us-rejected-judges-role.html) the ICJ was "not equipped" to
rule on complex international military issues; the administration went on to
[veto](https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1986/08/01/us-vetoes-
nicaraguan-resolution-on-compliance-with-court-
decision/ecdf20d6-cf3a-4761-ba23-5c49a9fa379a/) UN resolutions calling for
compliance with the judgment, rebelling against an institution that Netanyahu
had for years lambasted as "incapable" of handling terror threats.

The episode is just one example of how the United States would utilize
Netanyahu's blueprint for a permanent "war on terror," with increasingly
disastrous consequences for Americans and millions all over the globe.

### Rising Costs

It's been nearly eight months since the U.S.-Israeli War on Iran first began,
commencing with a horrific U.S. [strike](https://zeteo.com/p/100-days-and-
still-no-answers-for) on a school that killed more than 120 children. All
told, thousands of Iranians have been killed. At least 21 U.S. service members
have been [killed](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/10/us/politics/pentagon-
casualties-iran-war.html) with 865
[injured](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/10/us/politics/pentagon-casualties-
iran-war.html). As a result of the war, global energy prices have spiked.

While there is a ceasefire between Israel and Iran, the war between the U.S.
and Iran is ongoing, and the U.S. and Israel are apparently
[planning](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/21/us/politics/us-israel-renewed-
iran-strikes.html) to re-escalate after the forthcoming Israeli and American
elections.

The failed and illegal war, unpopular in the U.S. from the start, has crippled
Trump's [approval](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/10/21/politics/cnn-poll-trump-
democrats-republicans-midterms) ratings, threatening to cost Republicans in
the midterms.

In Israel, on the other hand, the war has been popular. Netanyahu instead is
weathering domestic disapproval for other reasons. There are the longstanding
allegations of corruption. There are the accusations he failed to stop October
7 despite being
[warned](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/06/nx-s1-5991630/israelis-grapple-with-
reports-that-netanyahu-was-warned-of-oct-7-attacks-years-ago) of looming
attacks. There are the allegations that he failed to rescue hostages from
Hamas, and that his government deliberately killed people on October 7 through
the ["Hannibal Directive."](https://zeteo.com/p/what-is-the-hannibal-
directive-and) There are also complaints that he's not doing _enough_ genocide
in Palestine.

Now, as the Israeli election approaches, I reviewed Israeli Prime Minister
Benjamin Netanyahu's decades-old writings, and the exclusive conferences and
meetings with D.C. elites he hosted, and congressional archives, and found how
extensive - and successful - his efforts have been to define "terrorism" in
Western power circles, and consequently, how influential he has been in
steering the American-led "War on Terror," including on Iran.
